correctness.rationale: A completely determined finite graph has 24 edges. An independently checked 11,393-face complex and exact deterministic 5,690-pair acyclic face-poset matching produce 1 critical vertex, 5 four-cells and 7 five-cells. The 55,256-incidence Hasse orientation passes a complete topological sort. Integral signed gradient reduction gives a specific five-by-seven attaching matrix with rank three, every four-minor zero and a unit three-minor (Smith factors 1,1,1). By Hurewicz and unit cellular cancellation the resulting CW complex is exactly two four-spheres and four five-spheres wedged together. Original mod-two Betti numbers independently agree; no infinite extrapolation is made.

originality.rationale: The 2026 Agarwal–Basak preprint explicitly asks for ordinary Möbius-ladder matching-complex homotopy in its Problem 26 (printed page 17), while its actual Main Theorem 1 covers a graph independence complex and a strictly smaller perfect-matching subcomplex. Its perfect-matching result at sixteen graph vertices is two three-spheres and cannot imply the computed ordinary mixed four/five-dimensional type. Bayer–Jelić Milutinović–Vega cover noncyclic polygonal *lines*, not twisted cyclic Möbius ladders, and establish only a qualitative sphere-wedge dichotomy for their family. Published finite results on the eight- and ten-vertex ladders and the different Möbius–Kantor graph do not imply the sixteen-vertex statement. Actual searches under equivalent graph/complex terminology found no covering result, with residual risk of an unindexed equivalent calculation.
residual_risks: An equivalent unindexed or not yet publicly discovered exact M16 ordinary-matching-complex calculation might exist.

value.rationale: The 2026 Agarwal–Basak Problem 26 expressly asks for the ordinary matching complexes of Möbius ladders, beyond its already classified graph independence and extendible/perfect matching complexes. The sixteen-vertex cubic example is a natural finite instance whose nonzero homotopy appears in two adjacent dimensions, unlike the perfect-matching counterpart. Computing integer attaching degrees, rather than an Euler characteristic or mod-two Betti numbers, is necessary and furnishes an exact reproducible structural result for future classifications.
